cards.explanation: The answer is that she becomes queen in place of Vashti. The attendants say it plainly: “Then let the young woman who pleases the king become queen in place of Vashti.” (Esther 2:4) Vashti is the queen being replaced. So this plan isn't just a talent show, friends. The winner gets the crown.

The answer is True. The text says it straight: “This suggestion pleased the king, and he acted accordingly.” (Esther 2:4) King Xerxes hears the plan and says yes. I wish my own ideas got that kind of green light.

The answer is that she has no father or mother. Esther 2:7 says Mordecai brought her up “…because she did not have a father or mother.” Mordecai is the Jewish man from the tribe of Benjamin, and Esther is the daughter of his uncle. So she's his cousin, and he takes her as his own daughter. That's what family does.
The answer is False. Esther 2:7 says Mordecai “…had taken her as his own daughter.” That's a daughter in the house, not a servant. Esther lost her parents, and Mordecai made room for her.

The answer is that Hegai shows her favor. Hegai is the king's eunuch in charge of the women, and he takes to Esther. Esther 2:9 says she “…pleased him and obtained his favor…” Then he gets busy on her behalf. Nice to have somebody in your corner, friends.

The answer is best. Esther 2:9 says Hegai “…transferred her with them to the best place in the harem.” Her seven select maidservants go along too. That's an upgrade with a whole team. I'd have been happy with a window that opens.
The answer is False. Esther 2:10 says, “Esther did not reveal her people or her lineage, because Mordecai had instructed her not to do so.” In the palace, she keeps both to herself.

The answer is that Mordecai told her not to tell. Esther 2:10 gives the reason: “…because Mordecai had instructed her not to do so.” Mordecai is the one who raised her, and she listens to him. The verse doesn't say why he gave the instruction, so I won't guess.

The answer is that he walks back and forth outside the harem court. Esther 2:11 says, “…every day Mordecai would walk back and forth in front of the court of the harem…” He does it to learn about Esther's welfare and what's happening to her. I think a man who does that every single day cares a lot.

The answer is whatever she requests. Esther 2:13 says the young woman “…was given whatever she requested to take with her from the harem to the king’s palace.” The choice is left with her. The verse doesn't say what any woman asked for, so I'll leave that open. That's a generous send-off, friends.

The answer is True. Esther 2:14 says she “…would not return to the king unless he delighted in her and summoned her by name.” Two things have to be true: he delights in her, and he summons her by name. Nobody shows up twice by accident.

The answer is Hegai. Esther 2:15 says she asked for nothing “…except what Hegai, the king’s trusted official in charge of the harem, had advised.” She takes his advice and leaves it there. You know that friend who skips the long list and just trusts the one who knows? That's Esther here.

The answer is False. Esther 2:15 says, “…Esther found favor in the eyes of everyone who saw her.” EVERYONE. Not a few, not most, everyone. I've stood in a bakery line where I couldn't get three people to agree on a cookie, so that's a lot of agreeing.

The answer is True. Esther 2:17 says, “…the king loved Esther more than all the other women…” More than all the other women is a big statement, friends. It says she found grace and favor in his sight, too. That's why the crown goes to her.

The answer is the royal crown. Esther 2:17 says, “…he placed the royal crown upon her head and made her queen in place of Vashti.” Not on a pillow, not in a box, but on her head. Now it's official, and Vashti's seat has someone new in it.
The answer is a tax holiday. Esther 2:18 says the king “…proclaimed a tax holiday in the provinces…” I bet that one got a cheer. It comes with the banquet and the gifts.

The answer is False. Esther 2:20 says, “Esther still had not revealed her lineage or her people, just as Mordecai had instructed.” Even with the crown, she says nothing. She does what Mordecai told her.

The answer is Esther. Esther 2:22 says, “When Mordecai learned of the plot, he reported it to Queen Esther…” Mordecai is sitting at the king's gate, and Esther is the queen he brings it to. She's the one who carries it to the king.

The answer is True. Esther 2:22 says “…she informed the king on Mordecai’s behalf.” Mordecai learned of the plot and reported it to Queen Esther. She is the one who informs the king, and she does it for him.

The answer is that they're hanged on the gallows. I think this part is heavy, so I'll say it simply. Esther 2:23 says that after the report was investigated and verified, “…both officials were hanged on the gallows.” Bigthan and Teresh are the two who plotted against the king. The report had been checked first.

The answer is that it's written in the king's records. Esther 2:23 says, “…all this was recorded in the Book of the Chronicles in the presence of the king.” It's written down right in front of him. A line in the books, not a billboard. And the story isn't over, friends.
